claim: With the P1-SPhos precatalyst, elevated temperature of 70–110 °C may increase coupling yield relative to 30 °C at matched residence time and catalyst loading, provided degradation does not dominate.
falsification: Compare matched P1-L2 experiments at 110 °C and 30 °C at the same residence time and loading; repeated lower or equal yields at 110 °C would contradict the proposed temperature advantage under those conditions.

claim: At 90–110 °C, residence times of 300–600 s may give higher yield than 60 s at matched catalyst and loading if conversion continues faster than degradation.
falsification: Compare 600 s and 60 s at 110 °C with the same catalyst and loading; repeated equal or lower yields at 600 s across matched pairs would contradict the proposed advantage in those conditions.

claim: At 100–110 °C and 2.0–2.5 mol% loading, P1-XPhos or P1-RuPhos may outperform P1-SPhos for this heteroaryl coupling at matched conditions, because changing the electron-rich biaryl phosphine can alter catalyst activity or stability.
falsification: Matched tests at 110 °C and 2.5 mol% that consistently yield no more than P1-SPhos at the same residence times would contradict the proposed advantage under those conditions.

claim: For P1-Xantphos, 30–60 °C is unlikely to surpass the current 88.44% incumbent because reduced thermal activation may limit coupling within 60–600 s; the observed temperature contrast is only at 600 s and 2.5 mol%.
falsification: An in-scope P1-Xantphos experiment exceeding 88.44% yield falsifies the specific prediction that this region does not surpass the current incumbent.

claim: With the P1-SPhos precatalyst, increasing temperature from 30 to 110 degC will improve yield at matched residence time and catalyst loading if activation is rate-limiting and thermal degradation does not dominate.
falsification: A matched P1-L2 comparison at 30 and 110 degC with the same residence time and loading that gives lower yield at 110 degC would contradict the proposed local temperature relationship.

claim: At 70–110 degC, P1-XPhos or P1-RuPhos may produce yields exceeding 19.70% in this coupling because bulky electron-rich biaryl monophosphines can support aryl chloride activation; this is a provisional expectation, not an observed ligand advantage.
falsification: Matched P1-L1 or P1-L3 tests at 600 s, 110 degC and 2.5 mol% yielding no more than 19.70%, together with further representative in-scope nonimprovements, would challenge this proposed improvement region.

claim: For this coupling, the P2 chloride/XPhos precatalyst may produce a yield above 23.33% at 600 s, 110 degC and 2.5 mol%, because its activation or catalyst speciation may differ from P1 methanesulfonate/XPhos. The direction of this scaffold effect is uncertain; no P2 result has been observed.
falsification: A P2-L1 measurement at 600 s, 110 degC and 2.5 mol% at or below the matched P1-L1 result of 23.3325% would contradict the predicted improvement at that condition; representative additional P2 nonimprovements would challenge the broader guidance.

claim: For this fixed coupling, P1-PPh3 may be less likely to exceed the current 40.09% incumbent across the tested operating range than the more electron-rich P1-PCy3 system, although the evidence is limited to one matched point.
falsification: An unqueried P1-PPh3 experiment exceeding 40.09% would contradict the proposed low-improvement caution for that condition; repeated high yields at other conditions would challenge the broader scope.

claim: For P1-XPhos with the fixed substrates, DBU and THF/water, heating to at least 65 degC may improve conversion relative to 30 degC at matched residence time and catalyst loading, provided catalyst and boronic acid remain sufficiently stable.
falsification: Compare matched P1-L1 experiments at 30 degC and at least 65 degC; repeated lower or equal yields under heating would contradict the proposed improvement in the tested conditions.

claim: With P1-Xantphos and the fixed reactants, DBU and THF/water, temperatures from 30 to 60 degC are unlikely to exceed the current 87.87% incumbent because coupling may be slow; catalyst stability and activation remain uncertain.
falsification: An independently selected P1-L4 experiment at 30–60 degC exceeding 87.87% yield would falsify the stated prediction at that condition; multiple high-yield tests would undermine its regional generality.

claim: With P1-Xantphos and the fixed reactants, DBU and THF/water, temperatures from 30 to 60 degC are unlikely to exceed the current 87.87% incumbent because coupling may be slow; catalyst stability and activation remain uncertain.
falsification: An independently selected P1-L4 experiment at 30–60 degC exceeding 87.87% yield would falsify the stated prediction at that condition; multiple high-yield tests would undermine its regional generality.

claim: With P1-Xantphos and the fixed reactants, DBU and THF/water, temperatures from 30 to 60 degC are unlikely to exceed the current incumbent because coupling may be slow; catalyst stability and activation remain uncertain.
falsification: An independently selected P1-L4 experiment at 30–60 degC exceeding 88.19% yield would falsify the prediction at that condition; multiple high-yield tests would undermine its regional generality.

claim: Under the fixed DBU and THF/water conditions, the P1-RuPhos precatalyst can give useful yield across accessible residence times, temperatures and loadings for this heteroaryl coupling.
falsification: Reconsider this broad claim if at least three P1-L3 experiments spanning different conditions each yield below 20%, or if matched comparisons consistently show lower yield than alternative precatalysts.

claim: With P1-RuPhos at 85–110 °C, faster coupling may allow yields above the current 84.09% incumbent, although residence time and catalyst loading can alter the outcome.
falsification: Reconsider the high-temperature opportunity if three new in-scope experiments spanning residence times and loadings all fail to exceed 84.09% yield, or if matched lower-temperature tests consistently yield more.

claim: For P1-RuPhos at 90–110 °C, 350–600 s and 2.0–2.5 mol% catalyst, increased catalyst availability and reaction time may yield above 85.58%; the proposed relationship is uncertain because the available observations are not matched comparisons.
falsification: Reconsider the improvement claim if three new in-scope experiments spanning the available residence times and loadings all fail to exceed 85.58%, or if matched shorter-time or lower-loading comparisons consistently outperform them.

claim: With the specified boronic acid under otherwise matched conditions, the bromo heteroarene tends to give a higher product UV area percentage than the corresponding chloro heteroarene, consistent with more accessible oxidative addition; ligand and medium can change the outcome.
falsification: Across at least three matched ligand, base and solvent comparisons, revise this local claim if the mean bromo minus chloro product UV area is zero or negative in percentage points; a single comparison is insufficient to establish generality.

claim: For the specified heteroaryl triflate, pinacol boronate ester and aminoaryl di-tert-butylphosphine combination, product UV area will often fall below the current 89.74% incumbent across base and solvent choices. Incomplete boronate activation or catalyst compatibility could contribute, but this mechanism is untested.
falsification: Revise this local low-response claim if at least two independently chosen base/solvent conditions in the scope exceed 89.74% product UV area; test activation separately with matched boron-partner comparisons.

claim: For the specified heteroaryl triflate, pinacol boronate ester and aminoaryl di-tert-butylphosphine combination, product UV area will often fall below the current 92.24% incumbent across base and solvent choices. Incomplete boronate activation or catalyst compatibility could contribute, but the mechanism is untested.
falsification: Revise the local low-response claim if at least two independently chosen base and solvent conditions in the scope exceed 92.24% product UV area; investigate activation separately through matched boron-partner comparisons.

claim: Under the fixed protocol, para-trifluoromethyl aryl iodide combinations will generally give higher reported amination yields than matched para-trifluoromethyl aryl chloride combinations because oxidative addition may be easier; additive and base effects may override this trend.
falsification: With at least four matched ligand, additive and base comparisons, reject the proposed local advantage if the median iodide-minus-chloride yield is zero or negative in percentage points; repeated in-scope yields below 10% would also challenge the absolute forecast.

claim: Under the fixed protocol, the supplied 3-iodopyridine can give high reported amination yields across some ligand, base and additive combinations, although heterocycle coordination or inhibition may strongly alter the outcome.
falsification: Challenge the high-yield generalization if at least three further independently selected in-scope conditions have a median reported yield below 60%; matched additive and base comparisons are needed to identify individual effects.

claim: Under the fixed protocol, combinations with the supplied para-trifluoromethyl aryl iodide tend to yield below the current 94.55% incumbent, although ligand, base and additive may change this outcome.
falsification: Challenge the low-yield generalization if at least two of four further independently selected in-scope conditions exceed 94.55% reported yield; matched conditions are needed to establish a substrate effect.

claim: Under the fixed protocol, combinations with the supplied para-trifluoromethyl aryl iodide tend to yield below the current 94.55% incumbent, although ligand, base and additive may change this outcome.
falsification: Challenge the low-yield generalization if at least two of four further independently selected in-scope conditions exceed 94.55% reported yield; matched conditions are needed to establish a substrate effect.

claim: At substrate concentration at least 0.3 mol/L, temperature at least 80 degC, and residence time at most 1.2 min, sufficient substitution may occur for high throughput to produce higher STY than otherwise comparable lower-temperature or longer-residence conditions; selectivity and conversion may instead limit this advantage.
falsification: Compare matched conditions differing in temperature or residence time: repeated lower STY within this region than the matched outside-region conditions would contradict the proposed advantage; report conversion or selectivity if available to distinguish causes.

claim: At 0.5 min and 0.5 mol/L, a lower temperature of 30–68.57 degC with 2.7–5.0 equivalents of pyrrolidine may yield STY above the current incumbent, if conversion and selectivity remain sufficient despite the shorter reaction time. The observed increase toward 68.57 degC is confounded by changes in temperature and equivalents and does not establish either causal effect.
falsification: Repeated measurements in this region below 10695.1 kg m^-3 h^-1 would contradict the proposed incumbent-beating advantage; matched comparisons across temperature and equivalents would separately test their effects.

claim: At 0.5 mol/L 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene, 3.28-5.0 equivalents of pyrrolidine and 30-42.86 degC, residence times of at least 0.714 min may yield lower STY than otherwise matched 0.5 min conditions: any gain in product formation may not offset the longer residence time. This is a provisional process expectation; the available longer-time comparison also changes pyrrolidine equivalents.
falsification: Compare matched pairs at 0.5 min and a longer in-scope residence time with identical equivalents, concentration and temperature. Repeated longer-time STY exceeding the matched 0.5 min values would contradict the proposed relationship; an in-scope observation above 11509.91 kg m^-3 h^-1 would also defeat the current-incumbent suppression rationale.

claim: If filling and transfer are effective and detector response is unsaturated, a sample loop of 0.05–0.08 mL can yield greater peak area than a smaller loop under otherwise comparable conditions.
falsification: Compare replicated or closely matched smaller- and larger-loop conditions; consistently lower or indistinguishable peak area for larger loops would challenge the claimed advantage in the tested range.

claim: If transfer completion limits the measured peak, waiting 8–10 s may improve peak area relative to shorter waits at otherwise comparable injection settings.
falsification: Closely matched or replicated longer- versus shorter-wait experiments that consistently show no increase in peak area would challenge this relationship over the tested settings.

claim: If draw rate affects reliable loop filling, sample flow of 1.0–1.6 mL/min may produce larger peak areas than slower draw rates under otherwise comparable transfer conditions. The observed association is confounded by other settings.
falsification: Replicated or closely matched comparisons showing no increase in peak area at 1.0–1.6 mL/min compared with slower flows would challenge the claim over the tested settings.

claim: If rapid pushing reduces effective sample transfer, push frequencies of 120–150 Hz may produce lower peak areas than 85–100 Hz under otherwise comparable filling and transport conditions. The observed differences are confounded by other settings.
falsification: Closely matched or replicated comparisons in which 120–150 Hz consistently gives peak areas at least as high as 85–100 Hz would challenge this relationship in the tested conditions.
